page: Amazon Web Services r8i.96xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors with 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The CPU provides a substantial 480 MB L3 cache alongside hardware instructions including AVX-512, AMX-TMUL, and AMX-INT8 matrix accelerators. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The server does not bundle local storage disks or hardware GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate superior multi-threaded computational and throughput capabilities. In multi-core CPU evaluations, the r8i.96xlarge achieves top-tier results in stress-ng (415,094.05) and PassMark CPU score (177,337.20), reinforced by high results in cryptographic encryption and extended instructions. Uncached read memory bandwidth reaches 1,125.32 GB/sec with write bandwidth at 446.27 GB/sec. Data processing metrics are similarly strong, shown by 508.55 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 33,532.41 in PassMark database operations, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 1,713.51 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics sit closer to average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,118.89 and Geekbench single-core score of 2,112.0.

From an efficiency standpoint, the instance trades single-threaded execution speed for massive parallel capacity and memory density. While CPU-based LLM token generation rates trail specialized accelerators (recording 34.24 tokens per second on a 135M model and 4.6 tokens per second on a 70B model), LLM prompt processing remains strong across model sizes due to memory bandwidth and matrix instruction sets. Because local storage is absent, persistent storage requires external network volumes. The r8i.96xlarge is best matched for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis clusters, big data ETL pipelines, distributed real-time analytics, and massive parallel compilation workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.96xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processors. It provides 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs at 3.9 GHz, supported by 3072.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (8.0 GB per core) and 480 MB of L3 cache. Network connectivity provides a 100 Gbps baseline, and the instance includes no local storage or GPUs. Benchmark results confirm top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in PassMark CPU marks of 177,337.20, Redis SET throughput of 508.55 million operations per second, and uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 1,100 GB/sec. While single-thread speeds and LLM token generation are moderate compared to specialized accelerators, its dense compute and memory capacity make it well suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching, massive software compilation, and large data processing pipelines.
